brief: UBS's flow desk says Friday's SPX -1.82% left Risk Control needing to sell $115-150bn, with $40-50bn done Friday and $75-100bn estimated for Monday. That Monday selling could deepen downside and trigger NQ1's remaining CTA close sell triggers, and only turns into heavier Tuesday selling if Monday's SPX drop exceeds -2%. Otherwise, Risk Control and CTA selling should fade, setting up a sharp recovery. Three Friday signals support that call. Nasdaq Excess Sell Flow was only -$8bn despite QQQ -3.5%, smaller than the S&P 500's already-modest -$24bn with SPY -1.8%, implying systematic selling was mostly absorbed by bargain-hunting. Late-day flow reversed to +$72bn of buying as UBS's retail flow (RMM) turned aggressive buyer from 2:45pm, concentrated in Tech ETFs and Semis/Memory. CTA exposure has fallen to the 13-19th percentile vs 3 years across ES1/NQ1/RTY1, leaving only NQ1 with close sell triggers left. Leveraged/inverse ETF rebalancing also needs to sell about $30.1bn, mostly in Nasdaq and Tech names.
